key_insight: Among the three detonation-sprayed WC coatings, WC–Co–Cr delivered the best overall hardness, friction, scratch resistance, and corrosion performance.
engineering_relevance: WC–Co–Cr coatings are promising for pipeline valves and other oil-and-gas components exposed to combined wear and corrosion.
method: Detonation-sprayed WC coatings with Co–Cr, Ni, and NiCr binders.
Characterized microstructure and composition using SEM and EDS mapping.
Measured microhardness, tribological behavior, scratch resistance, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: WC–Co–Cr achieved 1232.55 HV and a friction coefficient of 0.515, while WC–Ni had the lowest porosity (0.40%) and WC–NiCr the highest (2.78%); corrosion testing used 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term performance under representative valve service conditions, so application-specific validation is needed.
paper_title: Impact Of Co–Cr, Ni, and NiCr binder systems on the microstructure and functional properties of WC coatings produced by detonation spraying
